how: Do items in order. pages = PDF pages to read (inclusive); the article may start partway down the first page and the next article may start on the last page. chapter_guess comes from running heads: confirm it from the article's own title.

items.note: Question-by-question article: verse tags follow each question (v. 16, 12, 6, 1-17, 17, 16), so they go back rather than run straight through.

On 1:20 Denis discusses the Latin 'natum' ('born'), which the Douay-Rheims renders 'conceived': the lemma is marked with the Douay wording plus a translator's note; his discussion uses the literal 'born'. Is 8:3 is quoted in a variant form (Velociter spolia detrahe, cito prædare), marked with the Douay wording.

p. 22 (PDF 41): the edition prints 'circa quadringentos * annos' for the seventy weeks of Daniel; the footnote is not in the OCR, so the figure is kept and flagged in a translator's note. The closing mystical paragraph (three Magi, 'house of bread') is tagged v. 12.

Article runs pp. 26–30 (PDF 46–50), vv. 13–23. Denis's closing afterthought on the star is tagged v. 2, so the article header reads 'vv. 2–23'. Two quotations Denis gives in non-Vulgate form are translated without markers, with a translator's note: Is 11:1 'Nazaræus de radice ejus' (Hebrew, via Jerome) and Jerome's Septuagint reading of Num 23:22 ('Deus ex Ægypto vocavit eum; gloria ejus ut unicornis'). Matt 2:22: the Douay-Rheims file misspells 'Archclaus', so the name is kept outside the quotation marker.

Article runs pp. 31–40 (PDF 51–60), the whole of ch. 3. Three things to check against the scan: (1) p. 38 (PDF 58): the printed text gives 'Primo … prestaret… Tertio' with no second reason for Christ's baptism; kept, with a translator's note. (2) p. 34 (PDF 54): 'in Luca fertur Christum verba ista dixisse ad turbas', though in Luke 3:7 it is John who speaks; kept as printed, with a note. (3) p. 32 (PDF 52): 'de duris et crudis pellicearum minutiis' (John's girdle) is uncertain in the OCR. Denis reads 'ad radicem arboris' (singular) at 3:10, so the lemma marker stops at 'the root of the' and 'tree' follows outside it. The closing questions go back over the chapter (rebaptism tagged v. 6; the dove and the voice vv. 16–17).

Article runs pp. 40–46 (PDF 60–66), Matt 4:1–11; starts at the foot of PDF 60 (pre-split OCR: heading at the bottom of the left column). Two readings to check against the scan: (1) p. 42 (PDF 62): the Greek word after 'nomen Domini' is garbled in the OCR ('ceceayeziuxzov'); read as τετραγράμματον (same length, fits the sense). (2) p. 46 (PDF 66): 'Qui quia diabolus dicit se posse dare' kept as printed in the OCR, though 'Quæ' would fit better; translated by the sense. Eccles 3:21 and Prov 21:30 are quoted in variant forms (marked with Douay wording, translator's note gives Denis's reading). The closing moral paragraphs go back over the chapter (tags vv. 10, 1–3, 4–10, 8).

Article runs pp. 47–50 (PDF 67–70), Matt 4:12–25. Denis reads 4:16 as 'Populus qui ambulabat in tenebris' (Isaias 9:2's wording; Vulgate Matthew has 'sedebat'): marked with the Douay wording, 'walked' kept outside the marker, with a translator's note. p. 48 (PDF 68): the edition prints an asterisk after 'sedentibus' (footnote not in the OCR); kept as printed. OCR readings to check against the scan: p. 50 (PDF 70) 'Crebra namque et magna prodigia' (OCR 'lebra'), 'obtulerunt ei' (OCR 'et'). Matt 11:21 is quoted in reverse order ('Væ tibi, Bethsaida; væ tibi, Corozain') and the Douay-Rheims file reads 'Woe thee, Corozain', so 'to' sits outside the marker. The marginal reference for Josaphat reads 'I Par. xvii' in the OCR; the passage is 2 Par 17:7–9. The closing paragraphs (Jerome on the fishermen, the mystical sense of the four names, prelates visiting their flock) go back over the chapter (tags vv. 18–22, 18–22, 23).

Article runs pp. 51–59 (PDF 71–79), Matt 5:1–12 (the eight beatitudes); ends at the top of PDF 79, where Art. X begins. OCR readings to check against the scan: p. 54 (PDF 74) 'radio divinæ sapientiæ' (OCR 'radic'); p. 56 (PDF 76) 'ad ejus considerationem intellectum reducere' (OCR 'ac ejus'); p. 52 (PDF 72) 'visio Dei, qui ponitur tota merces' kept as printed. Where Denis reverses the order of a quotation (Matt 8:20 birds before foxes; Prov 15:27 'Per fidem et misericordiam') the marker keeps the Douay wording and order; for Prov 15:27 a translator's note says so. Variant forms marked with the Douay wording, with Denis's words outside the markers or in a note: Phil 3:8, 3:13–14, Phil 4:7 ('Pax Christi'), Is 25:1/4, Is 58:13–14, 1 Pet 2:20 ('Quæ enim gratia'), John 4:34 ('voluntatem Patris mei'). The closing question (is this the same sermon as Luke's?) is tagged vv. 1–12.
Art. X ends at v. 37 (Art. XI begins at v. 38 on PDF 90). In 5:14 the printed text calls Dionysius and the doctors 'lux illustrata, non illustrans'; translated as printed with a bracketed note.
Gaps from a misread line (a false heading split in the OCR) filled from the scan by hand on 2026-11-12.

Matt 24:27 in data/bible/drc reads 'cowling' for 'coming'; the quotation marker in 7:22 covers only the first half of the verse for that reason.
No pre-cut article file; assembled from PDF 118-124. Covers Matthew 8:1-13 (pp. 98-104).

Published (Matthew 9, Art. XVIII, all of ch. 9). PDF 136 (p. 116) is partly unreadable in the OCR: gaps marked […] at the end of the Eusebius statue story (v. 20), in v. 21 (one line), at the end of v. 22 (two lines, margin Deut. xxx, 4) and in the messengers' words to Jairus (v. 23). Please check against the scan. Tags whose margin note was unread or misread: Ps 84:9, 1 Cor 2:11 (margin read 'II Cor. i, 11'), Rom 8:30, Rom 10:3, Gal 4:4, 4 Kings 13:21, 3 Kings 17:21, 4 Kings 4:33; 1 Tim 1:15 (margin read as Luke 19:10). John 20:22 tagged where the margin prints xx, 23 (note in text). | 12 Nov: gaps filled from the scan by hand (the scan is clean; the OCR had dropped the lines).

Tags kept without a confirming margin reading (margin unread or misread): Is 1:14 (margin 'Is. i, 15'?), Mal 3:8 and 3:13 and Mal 4:5 (margin read as 'Mach'), Prov 26:11 (margin 'Prov. xxvi, 14'?), Matt 4:13 (margin 'iv, 16'?), Is 5:21, Is 47:10, Rom 9:22-23, Ex 33:19, Rom 9:18, Heb 2:8, John 13:5.

Ends with the lemma of 12:21 (bracketed in the OCR cut; check whether Art. XXIV repeats it). Tags kept without a confirming margin reading: Is 11:2, Is 55:4, Matt 25:34/41 (margins misread as Ps), Is 9:6 and Rom 1:4 (margin unread), Luke 23:11, Matt 21:1.

PDF 189 (p. 169) is partly garbled in the OCR: the last line of each column is lost (left: after 'et tamen falsatores pecu[niae]', Thomas on heretics; right: after 'beatitudo cae[lestis]', the treasure hidden in the field); gaps marked [...]. Margin unread or misread, tags kept: Is 53:10, Mal 4:2, 2 John 1:10 (margin seems to read 'Tit. iii, 10' there), 1 Cor 3:2. | 12 Nov: gaps filled from the scan by hand (the scan is clean; the OCR had dropped the lines).

PDF 274 (p. 254), v. 17: printed 'nec ob id quod in templo' — the sense seems to need 'nisi'; kept as printed with a translator's note. PDF 277 margin 'Exod. xl, 21' (v. 35) and PDF 277 'Cf. Prov. …' (v. 38) not identified; noted in the text.

Published. PDF 284 (p. 264): a crease or stain at the foot of both columns. Left column: one or two lines lost after 'Verumtamen, quantumcumque diu' (v. 22; probably 'duraret, non posset Dei propositum'), marked […] with a translator's note; right column: the line after 'Fecit signa magna, ita' restored from Apoc 13:13 ('ut etiam ignem faceret de cælo descendere in terram'). Check both against the scan. Also: data/bible/drc Matthew 24:27 reads 'cowling' for 'coming' (typo in the Douay-Rheims source).
